correctness.rationale: Along a planar free-boundary arc, orthogonal contact with the face forces the surface normal to be the planar unit normal to the curve, up to sign, so the plane-curve total absolute curvature equals the arclength of the Gauss image. The inspected exact representation proves that the Gauss map has degree one onto a spherical cuboctahedral square and identifies adjacent square vertices as \((1,0,-1)/\sqrt2\) and \((0,1,-1)/\sqrt2\). Their inner product is \(1/2\), hence the side length is exactly \(\pi/3\). The source's nonvanishing derivative formula on the open boundary side excludes flat subarcs, so each face arc is strictly convex. The argument distinguishes this boundary curvature from the already known Gaussian total curvature and does not include corner turning.

originality.rationale: The 2026 exact representation identifies the Gauss square and computes global Gaussian curvature, boundary length, and area, but does not state the Euclidean total curvature of one planar free-boundary arc. The full 1984 primary paper proves qualitative convexity and only an upper bound of less than \(\pi\) for the tangential-indicatrix length of each relevant trace piece. The present statement upgrades that classical qualitative information to the exact regular-tetrahedron value \(\pi/3\), using the newly available exact Gauss image. Targeted statement-level searches found no equivalent claim.

value.rationale: The physical free-boundary contact curves are a central geometric feature of Smyth's disk. Their exact turning is a natural scale-free invariant distinct from the surface's Gaussian total curvature and from its boundary length. The result upgrades Smyth's classical qualitative less-than-\(\pi\) control to the exact value \(\pi/3\) on every regular-tetrahedron face, proves strict convexity of each smooth arc, and ties the extrinsic boundary geometry directly to the newly explicit cuboctahedral Gauss image. This gives an exact consistency datum for analytic or numerical representations of the disk and a concrete geometric consequence of the 2026 closed form.
